narrative.northStar: The Block, Wired as One Hand-Bent Neon Circuit
narrative.overview: The system is an after-hours publisher threshold for four restaurant-game worlds. Ink-black enamel, exposed sign hardware, cobalt glass current, and warm electrode endpoints create the family identity. The design is restrained in chrome and expressive in subject matter, using flat countable geometry and precise typography rather than photorealism or generic game cards.
keyCharacteristics: Stable block topology with four structurally different doors.
Functional neon current used for selection and state.
Square enamel surfaces, one-pixel dividers, and visible hardware.
Condensed display lettering paired with high-legibility body copy.
Game color belongs to a restaurant; cobalt belongs to the group circuit.

rules.name: The Circuit Ownership Rule
rules.body: Cobalt identifies the group circuit; restaurant accents identify their own door and proof.

rules.name: The Fabricated Letter Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked display text belongs to labels and sign hardware; paragraphs use sentence case.

rules.name: The Enamel-First Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with tone, border, and overlap; glow belongs only to something visibly lit.

dos: Do keep the four doors stable while state and information change.
Do use game color locally and cobalt for shared circuitry.
Do preserve text equivalents for status, motion, and color-coded state.
Do author icons and diagrams as crisp SVG or CSS geometry.
Do keep source and availability language exact and repository-backed.
donts: Don't replace the block with a generic hero and equal feature-card grid.
Don't introduce rounded cards, glassmorphism, gradients, token tickers, or ambient neon around unlit objects.
Don't reuse one game's topology, instrument, cultural ornament, or tempo for another.
Don't turn ownership into the primary action or imply investment value.
Don't invent locations, hours, launch dates, testimonials, or playable availability.
